subject: App integration: sandbox warmup sprint & SDK quick-samples for Nimble Finance

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: App integration: sandbox warmup sprint & SDK quick-samples for Nimble Finance

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Per our conversation I've put together a short sandbox warmup plan and a tiny SDK sample bundle so your engs can hit our staging endpoints and exercise the common failure modes before the cutover. Attachments: nimble-mvp-map.xlsx (mutual action plan) and sdk-quicksamples.zip (Python + Go + curl examples).

Quick overview / asks:
- Sandbox access: we need one integration API key and a single test org id from you (reply with the token name and owner).
- Cutover window: propose a 45-minute canary on 2026-03-25 14:00 PT (we'll hold 14:00-15:30 for rollbacks).
- Readiness gates: unit tests passing, end-to-end smoke against /v1/generate, and a < 200ms median cold-start in staging for 1k requests.

Operational guidance (recommended defaults):
- Timeouts: client request timeout = 30s for standard completions. For streaming sessions: set per-chunk read timeout = 8s and an overall session timeout = 120s.
- Retries: 3 attempts on idempotent calls (0 -> 500ms -> 1s -> 2s exponential backoff) + random jitter +/- 100ms. Avoid retrying on 4xx.
- Rate limits: start with 60 requests/min per API key in staging to match expected production throttles; enable 429 handling with Retry-After header readout.
- Prefix/KV caching: if you plan to reuse shared prefixes across users, enable a 60s cache TTL for common prompts to reduce token throughput during warmup.

Cutover approach (high level):
1) Smoke in sandbox with export of 100 sample requests (capture latency/token counts).
2) Canary traffic (1% of production traffic to new endpoint for 10 minutes).
3) Observe cost/latency/quality metrics; if green, ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% in 10–15 minute steps.

Snippets in the zip show:
- Python: simple streaming consumer + backoff wrapper
- Go: client pool with per-call context timeout and token-bucket rate limiter
- curl examples: ephemeral token flow and regeneration pattern

I'll upload a short mutual-action-plan to Drive and drop the HubSpot record in the thread.

Thanks — please reply with the sandbox API key owner and whether the 3/25 slot works.

—
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn@redwood.com | x: 5403

Thanks, Evelyn — this looks actionable. A few clarifying Qs before we assign the sandbox key: 

1) Retry jitter: the suggested +/-100ms on top of exponential backoff — is that sufficient for noisy neighbor spikes if we hit 60 reqs/min? Our platform tends to burst during onboarding days.
2) Streaming timeout: you recommend 8s per-chunk and 120s overall. We have some long-response generation jobs ( > 60s). Is 120s the absolute max? Will the client see partial tokens if the session hits the overall timeout?
3) Can you include a short Go example that shows graceful cancellation when a user navigates away?

Also: we prefer to run the canary the morning slot 2026-03-25 09:00 PT if your team can make it — gives us time to react in our business hours.

On the 3rd-party side, we may need to request a temporary rate bump on day-of; can Redwood support a 2x throttling allowance for a 30-minute warmup window if needed?

Appended original for context.

Hi Maria —

Answers below and attached the updated bundle (sdk-quicksamples.zip) and the mutual action plan (nimble-mvp-map.xlsx). Links live here: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/nimble-warmup. HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/890

1) Retry jitter: +/-100ms is our low-risk default. For onboarding bursts we recommend increasing jitter to +/-500ms and using a capped backoff (max 2s) so retries spread without blocking. We'll include that variant in the Go sample.
2) Streaming timeout: 120s is our safety cap. For longer-run jobs we suggest using a session-resume pattern (persist kv-cache and resume stream with a new request) — this avoids single-session timeouts while preserving token continuity. The client will receive partial tokens up to the point of timeout; the Go/Python samples implement a resume key flow.
3) Go cancellation: Vanessa attached a short example that listens to context.Done() and gracefully closes the stream; it also emits a telemetry event you can use to map user cancellations to cost.

Canary timing: we can do 2026-03-25 09:00 PT — Vivek will be on rotation and will run the capacity sim one hour prior. Please confirm the sandbox API key owner and we will provision immediately.

Attachments: nimble-mvp-map.xlsx, sdk-quicksamples.zip, mutual-action-plan.md

Looking forward — small next step: Maria, please reply with the sandbox token owner and we’ll send creds.
